provenance.decision: IDEA-035 §6 and §10.1 (B1 adopted 2026-10-11): Class 1 Item 4.02 sells; Class 2 Items 1.05 and 2.06 block new buys for 5 sessions, then the block expires; Class 3 statements stay SHADOW (B2). D-11: only verified 8-K items on a held name may force an exit; the LLM only assesses.
provenance.record_design: IDEA-032 S1 (versioned predicate record: factual condition, issuer, affected period, required sources and fields, action map, block/reset/re-entry, fixtures) and IDEA-018 §4.4 (item code from the submissions JSON plus verified text). An accession plus an item code is not enough: the item's own section must assert the issuer's current occurrence.
provenance.written_by: IDEA-041 (Yao Zhu build record), 2026-10-11. Reviewer: Keith (I8).
provenance.parameters: max_event_age_ms is an IDEA-041 engineering value (7 calendar days, about 5 US sessions, enough to cover a weekend and a short outage) so that a late-discovered or backfilled old event never authorizes action; the team confirms it at the Oct 22 cut line (B6). block_sessions = 5 is the team's B1 decision.
provenance.scope_limit: Foreign private issuers (6-K filers, e.g. SK hynix) have no 8-K item codes, so no red-flag class applies to them in v1.0; their keyword events stay ordinary evidence. Recorded as a known gap, not a silent omission.
provenance.authority: This file defines what each predicate means and what its action is. Whether a predicate acts at all is set by the strategy profile (red_flag_authority, larp/integration/contract.py); the default for every predicate is SHADOW.

predicates.factual_condition: The issuer's own current Form 8-K or 8-K/A lists Item 4.02 in the SEC submissions metadata, and the Item 4.02 section of the saved filing text asserts, without negation, attribution to another company or hypothetical framing, that previously issued financial statements of the issuer should no longer be relied upon.

issuer_scope.identity: The filing belongs to the registered issuer (CIK checked at ingestion) and the occurrence clause's actor is the issuer (the company, its board or audit committee), not a third party such as an investee or supplier.

required_sources: SEC EDGAR submissions JSON (items field) for the issuer's CIK
the filing's primary document, saved text with its SHA-256

affected_period.extracted: period phrases named in the verified clause (e.g. 'second quarter of fiscal 2027', 'year ended December 31, 2025')
affected_period.rule: Recorded for audit. The Class 1 action is issuer-level and does not depend on the period.

freshness.rule: An event whose filing acceptance is older than max_event_age_ms at the assessment cutoff, or that was ingested in BACKFILL mode, is STALE and authorizes nothing.

predicates.reset: Not applicable: the exit and the buy block last while the latch is unresolved. A further verified 4.02 finding is a new finding; it keeps the block.

resolution.text: The latch resolves only when every supporting record is superseded by a revision that was read completely and no longer carries the finding, or is withdrawn (IDEA-033 R25).

predicates.reentry: IDEA-035 A8: once the latch is resolved (EVIDENCE_LATCH_RESOLVED), the name is eligible again.

predicates.factual_condition: The issuer's own current Form 8-K or 8-K/A lists Item 1.05 in the SEC submissions metadata, and the Item 1.05 section of the saved filing text asserts, without negation, attribution to another company or hypothetical framing, that a cybersecurity incident affecting the issuer occurred (Item 1.05 is filed when the issuer determines the incident is material).

issuer_scope.identity: The filing belongs to the registered issuer and the incident clause's actor is the issuer, not a supplier, customer or other company.

required_sources: SEC EDGAR submissions JSON (items field) for the issuer's CIK
the filing's primary document, saved text with its SHA-256

affected_period.extracted: dates and period phrases named in the verified clause
affected_period.rule: Recorded for audit; the block does not depend on it.

predicates.reset: The block starts in the first session in which the policy accepts the verified finding and lasts 5 sessions, then expires; the finding stays logged. A new verified finding on an original 8-K restarts the block. An 8-K/A (amendment) never restarts a running block; it starts one only if no block for this predicate and issuer has been started.

resolution.text: As for RF1-ITEM-4.02; a resolved latch also ends a running block (A8).

predicates.reentry: No forced sale. Buys are allowed again after the block expires or the latch is resolved, whichever comes first.

predicates.factual_condition: The issuer's own current Form 8-K or 8-K/A lists Item 2.06 in the SEC submissions metadata, and the Item 2.06 section of the saved filing text asserts, without negation, attribution to another company or hypothetical framing, that the issuer concluded a material impairment charge is required or recorded one.

issuer_scope.identity: The filing belongs to the registered issuer and the impairment clause's actor is the issuer.

required_sources: SEC EDGAR submissions JSON (items field) for the issuer's CIK
the filing's primary document, saved text with its SHA-256

affected_period.extracted: period phrases named in the verified clause
affected_period.rule: Recorded for audit; the block does not depend on it.

resolution.text: As for RF1-ITEM-4.02; a resolved latch also ends a running block (A8).

predicates.factual_condition: Event statements (risks, guidance, attributed claims, announced or future events) recorded in the evidence state's statement registry.

issuer_scope.identity: The statement registry of the issuer's evidence state.
